claim: With approximate (ANN) indexes pgvector applies WHERE filters after the index scan, so pre-0.8 a filter could leave too few rows; 0.8.0 iterative index scans keep scanning until enough results are found, exposed via hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order|relaxed_order|off (and ivfflat.iterative_scan) with limits hnsw.max_scan_tuples (default 20000), hnsw.scan_mem_multiplier and ivfflat.max_probes; partial indexes are the alternative for few distinct filter values. The pgvector/pgvector repo has about 21.7k GitHub stars.
quote: With approximate indexes, filtering is applied _after_ the index is scanned. ... SET hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order; ... SET hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order; ... SET hnsw.max_scan_tuples = 20000; ... SET ivfflat.max_probes = 100; ... If filtering by only a few distinct values, consider partial indexing

claim: pgvector 0.8.0 (released 2024-10-30) added iterative index scans as a technique to prevent overfiltering, continuing to search the index until a configurable threshold if the initial scan does not satisfy the query.
quote: iterative index scans, which is a technique to prevent 'overfiltering' or not returning enough results to satisfy the conditions of a query ... pgvector will continue to search the index until it hits a configurable threshold

claim: Pre-0.8 filtering ran after the index scan, so with default HNSW ef_search=40 a 10%-selective filter yielded roughly 4 usable rows; 0.8.0 iterative scans lifted recall on filtered queries from as low as 1-10% to 100% and gave up to 9.4x faster queries (123.3ms to 13.1ms).
quote: With default HNSW settings (ef_search = 40), if only 10% of data matched your filter, you'd retrieve roughly 4 usable results ... Category-filtered queries: 10% to 100% recall ... 9.4x faster results (Query A: 123.3ms to 13.1ms)

claim: strict_order guarantees results ordered by exact distance while relaxed_order allows slightly out-of-order results for better recall; relaxed_order is the recommended default and strict_order is used when ranking precision matters, with partial indexes recommended for category-specific searches.
quote: Strict order guarantees that the returned results are ordered by exact distance. Relaxed order allows results that are slightly out of order, but provides better recall ... Relaxed_order should be used by default, while strict_order should be used when ranking precision matters.

claim: A concrete hybrid pattern adds a STORED generated tsvector column (to_tsvector('english', content)) with a GIN index alongside an HNSW vector index, runs both searches, and fuses by reciprocal rank fusion with score 1/(k+rank), k=60, over-fetching ~20 candidates per side to return top 10.
quote: ADD COLUMN search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED; CREATE INDEX idx_chunks_search ON document_chunks USING gin(search_vector); ... RRF_score(d) = Σ 1 / (k + rank_i(d)) where k=60

claim: Hybrid search merges a vector ANN list and a lexical (BM25/tsvector) list with reciprocal rank fusion using the standard k=60 smoothing constant, combining rankings rather than raw scores so disparate score distributions need not be normalized.
quote: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), which combines rankings rather than raw scores, with each result getting a score of 1 / (k + rank) where k is a smoothing constant (usually 60)
